headline: Nuthatch 5.11.0 is a cold audit of 5.10.0 put right: 19 defects found by five readers on 2026-10-23, three of them high, every one fixed with a test that fails without it (#2353).

Nuthatch 5.10.0 adds `nuthatch watch`, a read-only view of a running nest (RFC-0069), and takes Burrmill forward four releases: a budgeted engine reads 2,048 rows at a time where it read 128, and an address is 20 bytes inside a plan rather than 42 characters.
Nuthatch 5.9.0 adds `nuthatch diff`: what happened in a block range, a block or a transaction, told in fixed sentences from the rows a nest already holds (RFC-0071).
Nuthatch 5.8.2 keeps a seal-direct backfill on a dense chain inside the per-cursor memory budget.
Nuthatch 5.8.1 refuses to reopen a store, or reuse its segments, after an event's indexed parameters have moved.
Nuthatch 5.8.0 is the cold audit of 5.7.2 put right: the 107 verified defects and the follow-ups found while fixing them, across six sprints (#2110).
Nuthatch 5.7.2 moves `init`'s output and a nest's identity into crates a browser tab can build, and names the chain head when an address-history range ends above it.
Nuthatch 5.7.1 stops a quiet table's last rows from being held back from the mirror indefinitely, and moves the sealing rule into a crate a browser tab can build.
Nuthatch 5.7.0 keeps an address-history nest answering when one part of its backfill cannot, and says in `/ready` how far each kind of data is served.
Nuthatch 5.6.3 makes the SQL memo hold what it counts.
Nuthatch 5.6.2 changes how the release is built, not what it builds.
Nuthatch 5.6.1 gives each watched account its own backfill pace.
Nuthatch 5.6.0 serves account history for several chains at one address, so rotki, which takes one indexer endpoint, can ask a single `nuthatch dev` about Ethereum, Base and Gnosis at once.
Nuthatch 5.5.0 serves account history on six more chains: Optimism, Base, Arbitrum, Polygon, BNB Chain and Gnosis, the chains rotki users are asked to buy explorer keys for.
Nuthatch 5.4.1 corrects what the deposit sweep's feed counts as a deposit.

Nuthatch 5.4.0 adds the deposit sweep (RFC-0064): an address-history nest that reads each block once for its whole watched set, so its cost is per block rather than per address, and delivers incoming transfers as one numbered feed with retractions when a reorg takes one back.
Nuthatch 5.3.3 lets an address-history backfill grow its windows over an RPC whose calls are slow whatever their range, and replaces a Polygon default endpoint that stopped serving logs.
Nuthatch 5.3.2 makes an address-history nest's first backfill finish in minutes over a hosted RPC, and stops it reading every block body for accounts nobody asked about.
Nuthatch 5.3.1 keeps an address-history nest serving through a long pass, and refuses a timestamp or a cached transaction that belongs to another fork.
Nuthatch 5.3.0 proves which blocks a validator proposed (RFC-0063 plan C), whoever received their fees, so rotki can book a validator's produced blocks and MEV from a nest alone.
Nuthatch 5.2.0 makes address history (RFC-0063) meet rotki's sync on Ethereum mainnet: history up to the chain head on demand, reorgs taken back, and answers that are exact or refused.
Nuthatch 5.1.1 fixes address history (RFC-0063) off Ethereum and makes its backfill workable on providers that cap a call's block range.
Nuthatch 5.1.0 adds address history (RFC-0063): a nest that watches accounts rather than contracts, and serves their history at `/api` in Etherscan's shapes, so rotki can use it as an indexer.
Nuthatch 5.0.1 is the first published 5.x release.
Nuthatch 4.15.2 changes one default: a nest started without `--poll-interval` now asks for the tip every 5 minutes instead of at the chain's block time.
Nuthatch 4.15.1 fixes one wrong answer in the GraphQL surface of the `graph` build: a filter on a `Bytes` field with a checksummed address matched nothing.
Nuthatch 4.15.0 adds the head count: after a successful `nuthatch init`, Nuthatch asks once whether it may count you.
Nuthatch 4.14.0 adds maintained views, keeps a view's own ORDER BY, and fixes two pieces of release tooling.
Nuthatch 4.13.0 is an engine release: a page taken over a chain of left joins no longer computes every row first.
Nuthatch 4.12.0 makes the query engine cheaper on view-heavy nests, adds Linux arm64 downloads, and fixes a shutdown that could hang.
Nuthatch 4.11.0 is the release the subgraph stopgap needed: a nest that answers a subgraph's own client queries can now be run from release downloads alone.
Nuthatch 4.10.1 fixes four defects.
Nuthatch 4.10.0 makes the engine count the memory a scan holds, so a nest's 2 GiB budget can be met by its own settings and enforced by its own startup check.
Nuthatch 4.9.0 lets a nest start from another operator's published history instead of backfilling it over RPC.

Nuthatch 4.8.0 makes a first run reach its data in seconds, keeps a published mirror consistent with what it holds, lets an operator finalise an archive nest's last segments, and makes the exact float sum cheaper.

Nuthatch 4.7.0 undoes a slowdown 4.6.0 brought to joins on computed keys, stops a pool with a throttled endpoint from retrying one range forever, prints dates and timestamps as dates, and stops a narrow window from counting a sealed block's rows twice in the derived views.
Nuthatch 4.6.0 makes floating-point sums reproducible, adds an opt-in table of Arbitrum's L1 block numbers, and fixes a memory overcharge and a slow walk over long empty ranges.
Nuthatch 4.5.0 adds a sampled audit of sealed history against a second endpoint, and a per-entity gauge of the memory DBSP holds for authored incremental entities.
Nuthatch 4.4.1 fixes wrong answers.

Nuthatch 4.4.0 brings a nest's serving process inside its 2 GiB budget under production's real load, makes kittiwake's one-day QoS statements about seven times faster, and closes the races found while testing it.
Nuthatch 4.3.1 fixes a wrong answer in 4.3.0.
Nuthatch 4.3.0 fixes the remaining ways Burrmill could run out of memory or refuse under a budget.
Nuthatch 4.2.1 rebuilds the built-in admin page so that an operator can see the whole of a running nest from a browser.

Nuthatch 4.2.0 fixes the memory regression that took the Lodestar allocations nest down on 2026-10-03, closes the rest of the confirmed audit findings, and brings Burrmill's answers closer to DuckDB's.
Nuthatch 4.1.1 closes the blocker and every high from the cold audit of 4.1.0, taken the day after the SQL engine changed.
Nuthatch 4.1.0 changes the SQL engine.
Nuthatch 4.0.2 fixes how one RPC error is read.
Nuthatch 4.0.1 replaces the two public Ethereum mainnet endpoints a new nest is given, because neither could serve a backfill.
Nuthatch 4.0.0 is the stable line.
Nuthatch 3.13.3 makes `nuthatch check` tell the truth about incremental entities, and fixes what that uncovered.

Nuthatch 3.13.2 is the result of a hardening pass over what 3.13.1 already does: a new user's path from install to first query, the SQL surface under inputs it should refuse, crash recovery, and measured performance, run against Arbitrum One and Base.

Nuthatch 3.13.1 fixes what an end-to-end run of 3.13.0's runtime admin API found against a real chain: three ways a runtime could be left unable to restart, a move that broke a dataset two tenants shared, identical mounts sent together that reported a live nest as failed, and a runtime whose metrics were reachable only through one of its mounts.
Nuthatch 3.13.0 lets a runtime run its own nests' lifecycle.

Nuthatch 3.12.2 moves the WASM runtime past two security advisories, holds a nest mounted on a running runtime to the rules boot already enforces, finishes the 504 for a spent query budget that 3.12.1 began, reads two GraphOps RPC responses correctly, and lets a runtime start with nothing mounted.
Nuthatch 3.12.1 fixes one performance fault on the `/sql` surface and changes how one failure is reported.
Nuthatch 3.12.0 changes nothing in the published binaries.
Nuthatch 3.11.0 is about the RPC bill.
Nuthatch 3.10.0 is a small release with one change that matters when upgrading.
Nuthatch 3.9.0 adds `nest nid`, which prints the identity a nest's data is stored under, and `offchain pull`, a one-shot fetch that seals a price feed as an offchain snapshot.
Nuthatch 3.8.5 fixes two correctness faults in the analytics surface.
Startup refuses a store whose data no longer matches what `nuthatch.toml` covers, and `/` and `/nest` show the nest's `nid` and `data_identity` (#1423, fixes #1420).

A runtime now keys a nest's cursor, health and metrics by the route it serves the nest under, so a nest whose route differs from its name is measured, quarantined and unmounted correctly (#1419, fixes #1415).
Fixes a `--seal-direct` backfill over `[[ipfs]]` documents that paused without a word on a slow gateway (#1399).
Fixes a delay encountered while backfilling Edge & Node's QoS oracle with 3.8.0.
The release that makes an `[[ipfs]]` nest over megabyte documents fit to deploy.
The first release since the 2026 feature freeze ended on 2026-09-08 (#1231), and the first built from the programme that replaced it.
One fix, on a defect that had two production nests reporting perfect health while the watermark their receipts pin had not moved in two days.
The release that makes a dashboard cheap to serve.
A patch for the two things the Lodestar cutover found on 2026-09-06.
The release that turns the RPC bill down.
Three things found on one afternoon of running a fresh 3.4.0 nest behind a live dashboard.
Sparse tables stop fanning out into one tiny file per seal cut, and Robinhood Chain is built in.
One fix, to what every nest asks for and seals.
A new built-in chain, and a fix to the front door.
Two changes to the binary, one of which an operator should read before restarting, and a good deal of tooling around the edges.
A security update, two production defects that only measurement could have found, and a sprint's worth of gates that turned out not to be gating anything.
A one-line fix to a metric, and a great deal of measurement that changed what we believe about our own system.
Authored incremental entities, stable.
A patch release for the operational work that landed after 2.7.1.
A fix release.
A nest that declares `[[calls]]` can use `--seal-direct` again, a factory nest stops aborting its backfill on a provider cap, and this page stops quoting performance numbers it cannot stand behind.
The first run stops stalling.
The front door.
A fix release.
The release that closes subgraph parity.
Twenty-seven commits since 2.4.0.

Upgrading is a binary swap.

Be your own indexer.
Be your own indexer.
Scaffold a nest from a subgraph manifest.
Be your own indexer.
A security fix, and scaled mode's writer pool starts writing.
v0.9.1 described a fix its binary did not contain.
Two fixes, one of them a security advisory.
RFC-0029 is complete.
Backfills on Alchemy no longer die, and the slowest part of a backfill got faster.
Scaled mode's compose deployment actually works now.
Scaled mode: nuthatch across machines.
A nest that indexes nothing now says so, and the last unstarted RFC has started.
A packaging fix.
Security patch.
Audit hardening patch.
Portable, distributable, multichain, derive-first.
The delightful, agent-native release.
Turn any contract into a local SQL database.
